## Dedicated servers: catalogue, pricing, managed machines, previews (2026-10-06, branch `feature/dedicated-servers`)

Resold bare-metal, built so the owner can review everything before customers see any of it. **Unreleased by default**: Setting `dedicated_public_enabled` is `false`, so `/dedicated-servers` and `/dashboard/dedicated/**` 404 for everyone except **private-preview accounts** (see "Private preview + online checkout" below; fail closed if settings cannot be read) and the sitemap does not list them. Admins review both at `/admin/preview/dedicated` and `/admin/preview/dedicated/dashboard`. The portal rail shows a "Dedicated" entry only to viewers who pass the gate.

**Brand voice.** Customers never see the supplier's name, ranges, plan codes, service names, datacenter codes or URLs. Upstream identity lives only in admin pages and in `lib/dedicated/ovh-catalog.ts` / `sync.ts` / `catalog-view.ts`. Customer components (`components/dedicated/**`, the two customer route trees) only read `lib/dedicated/customer-view.ts` projections. Those projections copy a field whitelist, pass free text through `brandSafe()`, and hide the supplier's default `nsNNN.ip-a-b-c.tld` hostname. `test/dedicated-brand-voice.test.ts` checks the source files and the real output built from recorded catalogue fixtures.

**Catalogue sync** (`lib/dedicated/sync.ts`; worker sweep `dedicated-catalog`, 1-minute wake, self-throttled; admin "Sync now"; `npx tsx scripts/dedicated-catalog-sync.ts [SUBSIDIARY]`):
- **Read-only.** Three anonymous GETs and no API keys: `/order/catalog/public/eco` and `/order/catalog/public/baremetalServers` (`?ovhSubsidiary=`), plus `/dedicated/server/datacenter/availabilities`. The host follows the subsidiary: WE/WS/ASIA/CA/... use `ca.api.ovh.com`, US uses `api.us.ovhcloud.com`, the EU subsidiaries use `eu.api.ovh.com`. `publicGet` refuses any other path. The default subsidiary is `WE` (our account's own, USD). Upstream prices are in units of 1e-8 of the currency, so cents = price / 1e6.
- **Data.**
  - `DedicatedCatalogItem` holds one row per upstream plan. Regional variants (`-sgp`, `-syd`, `-mum`) are separate plans with their own price.
  - `DedicatedCatalogOption` holds the memory, storage, system-storage, bandwidth, vrack and GPU choices, each with its extra monthly cost. Licences are skipped.
  - `DedicatedAvailability` is the stock snapshot per plan, memory and storage configuration and datacenter.
  - `DedicatedCatalogSync` records every attempt with its counts, warnings and errors.
- **Keep last good.**
  - Each catalogue is fetched, parsed and written independently. A parse that returns less than 30% of the plans we hold is treated as an upstream glitch, not as a mass removal. Plans that disappear get `removedAt` and are never deleted.
  - The stock snapshot is replaced in one transaction, and only when the new feed is plausible.
  - A plan can be listed in both catalogues (the Advance range is). The first catalogue in the run owns it.
- **Nxeon-owned columns** are never touched by a sync: `visible` (default false), `displayName`, markup overrides, `overrideMonthlyCents`, setup policy, `hiddenRegions` and `adminNote`.
- **First live run (2026-10-06, WE).** 240 unique plans (eco 99, baremetalServers 165, with overlap), 4,851 options and 36,294 stock rows. By range: Kimsufi 27, So you Start 13, Rise 35, Advance 42, Game 2, Scale 73, HGR 48. Datacenters: gra, fra, bhs, rbx, sbg, waw, lon, sgp, syd, ynm, eu-west-par-a/b/c and ca-east-tor-a, all mapped.

**Regions** (`lib/dedicated/regions.ts`) map upstream DC codes to Nxeon codes in the `lib/node-regions.ts` style: sgp→sgp1, bhs→bhs1, gra→gra1, rbx→rbx1, waw→waw1, fra→fra1, lon→lon1, sbg→sbg1, syd→syd1, ynm→bom1, vin→vin1, hil→hil1, ca-east-tor-a→tor1, eu-west-par-a/b/c→par1/2/3.
- Each region has an admin label and a customer label.
- `sold` means Nxeon already runs nodes in that metro (sgp1, bhs1).
- An unknown code maps to `unmapped:<code>`. It is flagged in the sync log and the admin catalogue, and nothing breaks.
- The regions where dedicated servers are offered come from Setting `dedicated_enabled_regions`. Default (owner decision 2026-10-06): **every mapped region**; only in-stock configurations are orderable. Untick regions on `/admin/dedicated/pricing`. (An existing Setting row from an earlier save keeps its old value.)

**Pricing** (`lib/dedicated/pricing.ts`, pure, `test/dedicated-pricing.test.ts`):
- The Nxeon price is `round(cost x (1 + markup%) + fixed)`. Every rounding mode rounds up: `ninety-nine` gives the next $X.99, and the other modes are `whole`, `five` and `none`.
- Item overrides win over the global rule. Options are marked up too, even on top of a hard override price.
- Setup-fee policy:
  - `pass` charges what the setup costs us now, including a live upstream promotion.
  - `waived` charges nothing.
  - `custom` charges a fixed fee.
- Settings: `dedicated_markup_percent` (25), `dedicated_markup_fixed_cents` (0), `dedicated_rounding` (ninety-nine), `dedicated_setup_policy` (pass), `dedicated_setup_custom_cents`. The defaults are placeholders pending the owner's decision.
- Cost, margin, first-year margin and setup payback are shown in admin only.

**Admin** (ADMIN role only; nav: Fleet → Dedicated servers):
- `/admin/dedicated` is the catalogue browser. It filters by text, range, region, minimum RAM, maximum price, in-stock, visible and removed, and shows the sync status and **Sync now**.
- `/admin/dedicated/catalog/[id]` is the item detail page:
  - the hardware, economics, upstream commitment terms and promotions;
  - each region's stock and offered/hidden flags;
  - the full stock matrix (memory x storage by datacenter) and every option with cost vs Nxeon price;
  - the Nxeon controls and "Create offer from this item".
- `/admin/dedicated/pricing` holds the rules, the offered regions (with "we have nodes" / "not sold yet"), the public-pages switch and a worked example table.
- `/admin/dedicated/servers` and `/admin/dedicated/servers/[id]` hold the managed machines (`DedicatedServer`):
  - Each record has the customer, frozen specs, Nxeon region, IPs, OS, renewal date/price/term, linked invoice ids, offer id, and **admin-only** fields (upstream service name, upstream DC, our cost, internal notes).
  - The manual lifecycle is PENDING → PROVISIONING → ACTIVE ⇄ SUSPENDED → CANCELLED. It **records state only**; staff do the real work by hand.
  - Credential delivery is encrypted with `lib/crypto-box`, and the customer reveals the credentials themselves.
  - Customer requests are listed with Done/Cancel.
  - The audit trail is `DedicatedServerEvent` plus `recordAudit`.
- **Offers link.** `lib/dedicated/offer-link.ts` builds a DEDICATED offer prefill (cores, RAM, disk, tier, region, price, setup; the upstream plan code goes in the staff-only internalNote only). The button is a disabled stub until the custom-offers feature (`feature/chat-offers`) merges, because `offersAvailable()` checks for the Prisma `Offer` model at runtime. **Follow-up when offers merge:** `/admin/offers` should read the `kind`/`catalogItem`/prefill query params into `OfferComposerForm`, and a PAID DEDICATED offer's DEDICATED_BUILD task should link to "Add managed server" (`/admin/dedicated/servers?item=<catalogItemId>`) and store `offerId`.
- **OVH admin-controls link.** `DedicatedServer.providerServiceName` has the same meaning as `Node.providerServerId`, so the `lib/ovh-admin` readers (branch `feature/ovh-admin-controls`) can render a live panel on the server page later. Nothing here calls the authenticated upstream API.

**Customer surfaces** (gated: public flag or private preview; admin-previewable):
- The public page (`components/dedicated/DedicatedMarketing.tsx` + `DedicatedCatalogGrid.tsx`) shows:
  - an asymmetric hero with a live entry-build spec plate;
  - live stock by offered region;
  - a filterable catalogue (tier, location, in stock, sort) with a per-region Nxeon price;
  - an honest "how it works" (quote → accept → keys), what's included, and a FAQ.
- Builds show "Configure", which opens the online checkout (`/dashboard/dedicated/order/<id>`, see below); "Ask for a custom build" still goes to `/contact?topic=dedicated`. A person builds every machine. Only items marked visible are listed; the admin preview (and a private-preview account) shows every live item when none is opted in yet.
- The customer dashboard (`components/dedicated/DedicatedServerDashboard.tsx`) shows specs, IPs (copy), status, region, a bandwidth "coming soon" placeholder (no fake graph), billing/renewal, invoices and login delivery (reveal).
- Reboot, reinstall and rescue are **requests**. `lib/actions-dedicated-customer.ts` opens a normal support ticket (`createTicketCore` + Discord mirror) and a `DedicatedServerRequest`. It is owner-checked, flag-checked and rate-limited. Preview buttons are inert.

**Deploy:** `prisma db push` adds 6 tables and 1 enum and changes no existing table. The worker picks up the sync sweep on restart, and the first sync runs within a minute. Nothing becomes customer-visible until the owner turns on `dedicated_public_enabled` (Pricing page switch).

Tests: `test/dedicated-catalog.test.ts` (recorded fixtures in `test/fixtures/dedicated/`), `test/dedicated-pricing.test.ts`, `test/dedicated-regions.test.ts`, `test/dedicated-gate.test.ts`, `test/dedicated-brand-voice.test.ts`.

### Private preview + online checkout (2026-10-06, branch `feature/dedicated-private-preview`)

**Private preview gate** (`lib/preview-access.ts`, shared verbatim with the AI mod builder branch, feature keys `dedicated` and `modbuilder`):
- `isPreviewUser(user, feature)` is true when the signed-in account's email is on the feature's allowlist. The allowlist is Setting `preview_access_emails_<feature>` if that row exists, else Setting `preview_access_emails` (shared by all features), else the code default `nicholas.sj.albanese@gmail.com` (the owner's own customer account). Comma/space separated, case-insensitive. An existing but empty Setting means nobody. Any DB error means nobody.
- `lib/dedicated/gate.ts`: `dedicatedAccessFor(user)` = public flag on OR preview user. `requireDedicatedAccess()` is the first await of every customer route (marketing page, `/dashboard/dedicated`, `/dashboard/dedicated/[id]`, `/dashboard/dedicated/order`, `/dashboard/dedicated/order/[id]`) and calls `notFound()` otherwise. Every customer server action (`lib/actions-dedicated-customer.ts`, `lib/actions-dedicated-order.ts`) re-checks it and answers "Not found".
- Signed-out visitors to `/dashboard/dedicated/**` are sent to login by the dashboard layout, exactly like any other (even non-existent) `/dashboard/*` URL, so nothing reveals the feature. `/dedicated-servers` 404s for them.
- No sitemap entry and `noindex` unless the PUBLIC flag is on (a preview never advertises). The portal rail entry (`lib/dedicated/nav.ts`, passed to `components/nx/Shell` as `extraNav`) is added only for viewers who pass the gate.
- To give another account access: Setting `preview_access_emails_dedicated` = `owner@…,qa@…`. To remove everyone: set it to an empty value. To launch: turn on `dedicated_public_enabled`.
- Preview catalogue: while NO catalogue item is marked visible, a preview account sees (and can order) every live item, with a banner saying so. Once any item is marked visible, only visible items are listed, for preview and public alike.

**Customer flow** (all portal-styled: `components/dedicated/order/*`, `components/dedicated/DedicatedServer*.tsx`):
1. `/dashboard/dedicated/order`: in-stock builds only (one card per hardware build; regional variants merged), filters for location (all regions listed, sold-out ones labelled), CPU brand, minimum cores, memory, storage and max monthly price, sort. Price = Nxeon price from the pricing rules (markup included). "Online within 24 hours" on every card.
2. `/dashboard/dedicated/order/[id]`: Configure — location (only in-stock locations selectable), memory, storage (combinations not in stock are disabled; picking one auto-switches the other to an in-stock partner), network (bandwidth options, when more than one exists), OS (`lib/dedicated/order-core.ts` `DEDICATED_OS`: Ubuntu 24.04/22.04, Debian 12, AlmaLinux 9, Rocky 9, Proxmox VE 9; installed by the handover job or staff), term (Monthly, or Annual = 12 x monthly up front, no discount because the pricing rules define none), optional name. Every price on this step comes from a server-computed price table (`loadOrderBuild`), the same function the charge uses.
3. Review — the server re-quotes (`quoteDedicatedOrderAction`): specs, location, OS, term, setup, tax (destination VAT via `taxContextForUser`, same as VPS), total today, renewal stated as charged (`$X/mo` or `$X/yr`), wallet toggle with the split.
4. Pay — the portal's standard wallet-then-card path: wallet covers it -> placed immediately; otherwise a Stripe Custom Checkout session (`createDedicatedOrderPaymentSession`, ui_mode `elements`, rendered inline by `components/nx/NxCardFields`) for exactly the card remainder. Metadata `nxeonDedicatedOrder` (intent) + `nxeonDedicatedOrderPrice` (stamped price). `lib/fulfil-checkout.ts` (`dedicatedOrder` branch) credits the card leg to the wallet, then `placeDedicatedOrder` debits the STAMPED total. Card-leg sessions are purchase legs (`isPurchaseLegSession`), so no duplicate top-up invoice. PayPal/crypto/local methods are not offered for dedicated orders yet.
5. The order lands as a `DedicatedServer` with status **PENDING**: frozen specs, region, OS label, `renewalMonthlyCents` + `termMonths`, renewal date (order date + term), setup fee, the PAID invoice id, and admin-only fields (`datacenter` with the best stock at order time, `costMonthlyCents`, `notes`, `orderConfig` JSON with the upstream plan/option codes). The customer gets an in-app notification; every ADMIN gets one linking to `/admin/dedicated/servers/<id>`, whose new "Online order — build this by hand" panel shows the full build sheet.
6. Customer dashboard `/dashboard/dedicated/[id]`: status timeline (Order received -> Being built -> Online), specs, IPs once assigned, login reveal, renewal ("$X/yr" for annual), invoices, support, request buttons once ACTIVE. `?ordered=1` shows the confirmation banner.

**Money safety.** One order key per checkout (client-generated) is claimed in `FulfilledSession` as `dedorder:<userId>:<key>`, so a double click, a retry, or the webhook/redirect race places at most one order and debits once. Wallet debit, wallet transaction, PAID invoice, server row, event and audit log are one transaction (spend caps honoured). A failed wallet placement releases the claim. A card-leg failure after capture is recorded FAILED and the customer is told the money is in their wallet (`notifyStalled`). Impersonating admins cannot pay. Unverified emails cannot pay (`emailVerificationError`).

**Not built (owner decisions).** Automatic renewal charging for dedicated servers (renewals stay manual, as before); partner/creator commission on dedicated invoices; PayPal/crypto for dedicated; an annual discount; cancellation/refund flow (staff, by hand).

**Schema (additive):** `DedicatedServer.orderKey String?` (indexed) and `DedicatedServer.orderConfig Json?`.

### Phase 2: automated actions on a delivered server (same branch)

Nxeon owns the machine upstream and keeps out-of-band control; the customer gets root inside the OS only (their own SSH key; nothing Nxeon-owned is installed in their OS). The customer never sees the supplier.

**Rule: nothing mutates from the web tier.** Customer/admin actions (`lib/actions-dedicated-ops.ts`, `lib/actions-dedicated-ops-admin.ts`) only validate and insert a `DedicatedJob`. The worker sweep `dedicated-jobs` (`worker/dedicated-jobs.ts`, every 10 s) is the only place an upstream write happens: it runs `lib/dedicated/ops.ts` `runJobStep` and, for the real upstream, sends every write through `lib/ovh-admin/write.ts` `ovhAdminWrite` (rights check, per-actor and per-target rate limits, AuditLog before and after). Every job end also writes a `DedicatedServerEvent` and an AuditLog row; a failure notifies every ADMIN.

**Modes.**
- `dedicated_ovh_dry_run` (Setting, **default `"true"`**): nothing is sent; jobs finish "Dry run: ...". The admin server page shows a DRY RUN / LIVE badge. Set `"false"` to go live.
- `NXEON_DEDICATED_OVH_MOCK=1` (ignored when `NODE_ENV=production`): a fake upstream (`lib/dedicated/ovh-mock.ts`, file-backed so web + worker share it) for demos; the customer panel shows a "Demo machine" badge.

**Safety.** The target is always `DedicatedServer.providerServiceName` from OUR row (customers pass only our server id). A service name equal to any `Node.providerServerId` (or listed in Setting `dedicated_ovh_protected_services`) is refused before any call, so a mistyped link can never touch a platform node. rDNS / firewall IPs must lie inside the blocks upstream reports for that service. Disruptive actions (reboot, rescue, reinstall, handover): one at a time per server, 6 per hour per server; 30 actions per hour per customer; typed confirmation (the server's name) for reinstall; blocked while impersonating.

**What the customer can do** (`components/dedicated/DedicatedControlPanel.tsx`, on `/dashboard/dedicated/[id]` once the server is ACTIVE and linked):
- Overview: power, boot mode, network port and traffic, detected hardware (GETs, cached 20 s).
- Hard reboot (`POST /dedicated/server/{sn}/reboot`, task polled). No soft reboot exists upstream; the panel says to use `sudo reboot` for a graceful restart.
- Rescue: netboot rescue with the customer's SSH key (`PUT /dedicated/server/{sn}` `{bootId, rescueSshKey}` + reboot), back to disk the same way. If staff ever get a rescue password, they store it encrypted on the admin page (`rescueSecretEnc`) and the customer reveals it (`decryptSecret`).
- Reinstall: images from `GET .../install/compatibleTemplates`, filtered and renamed (`lib/dedicated/ops-core.ts` `offerableTemplates`: no Windows/licensed, panel, BYOI or "withapp" images), hostname + one of the customer's SSH keys, typed confirmation, `POST .../reinstall` `{operatingSystem, customizations:{hostname, sshKey}}`, progress from `.../install/status` + the task. Nxeon adds no deploy key (the VPS flow injects only the customer's keys too).
- Reverse DNS (`POST /ip/{block}/reverse`), network firewall per IPv4: on/off, add/remove rules (`/ip/{block}/firewall/...`, validated by the existing `lib/ovh-admin/validate.ts` rules).
- Extra IPv4 (1, 4 or 8): priced from `dedicated_ip_price_cents`, prorated to the next renewal (`extraIpProrateCents`), paid wallet-then-card (Stripe metadata `nxeonDedicatedIpOrder`, fulfil branch `dedicatedIpOrder`). Lands as `DedicatedIpOrder` PAID. **Nothing is bought until an ADMIN clicks "Approve purchase"** on the server page; approval enqueues `IP_ORDER`, which creates an upstream cart, adds the IP product for that size routed to the server (`destination`, `country`), checks out with the account's payment method, waits for delivery, then adds the block to the server and the monthly price to `renewalMonthlyCents` (+ `extraIpMonthlyCents`). "Reject & refund" returns the full charge to the wallet.
- Remote console: **not shipped to customers.** The upstream only offers its own hosted KVM/SOL pages (`/features/ipmi/access`), so the panel offers "Open a ticket" and staff open the console.

**Handover (auto-install).** On a PENDING/PROVISIONING server, after staff buy the machine and save its service name, "Install & hand over" (admin server page) enqueues `HANDOVER`: install the OS the customer ordered (matched by label) with the customer's first SSH key, then mark ACTIVE, fill IPs from upstream, set hostname/OS, notify in-app and send the `dedicated_server_ready` email template (`prisma/seed-email-templates.ts`; never sent in mock mode). A customer with no SSH key: the button refuses; deliver credentials by hand.

**Schema (additive):** `DedicatedJob`, `DedicatedIpOrder`; `DedicatedServer.rescueSecretEnc`, `DedicatedServer.extraIpMonthlyCents`. Settings: `dedicated_ovh_dry_run`, `dedicated_ovh_protected_services`.

**Verified against real upstream (read-only GETs only, 2026-10-06):** server object fields (incl. `rescueSshKey`), rescue/disk boot ids, the compatible image list (used as a test fixture), `install/status` 404 when idle, hardware/network spec shapes, and that the IPMI feature exposes only hosted console URLs. `cartServiceOption` for our machines returned no IP options, so IP orders use the generic cart IP product; that path, and every write, is verified only against the mock (`test/dedicated-ops.test.ts`).

### Marketing page, nav and logos (same branch)

- **NXM page** `/dedicated-servers` (bare metal): native page `tools/nxm/native/dedicated-servers/` (+ `tools/nxm/wire/dedicated_servers.py`, loader `app/nxm/_data/dedicated-servers.ts`, route in `nxmlib.py` ROUTES, SEO entry in `app/nxm/_seo/registry.ts`, `live-routes.json` regenerated). Regenerate with `python3 tools/nxm/port_pages.py dedicated-servers`. Live in-stock catalogue rendered client-side from the loader's data (filters: location, AMD / Intel / GPU, cores, memory, storage, price); "Configure" goes to `/dashboard/dedicated/order/<id>` (signed out: `/register?next=...`). Hero art: `public/nxm/home/renders-rack.webp`.
- **Gate:** the loader calls `requireDedicatedAccess()` (404 otherwise); metadata is noindex unless public; `/dedicated-servers` is in the NXM sitemap `EXCLUDE` and is advertised only through `dedicatedSitemapPaths()` once public. The old `app/(marketing)/dedicated-servers` page (served when `NXM_ROOT` is off) has the same gate.
- **Nav:** `app/nxm/_components/dedicated-nav.ts` injects a "Dedicated" desktop tab, a Products-menu entry and a mobile-sheet link at render time (NxmPage + home), and a "Need more power?" strip before the FAQ on `/vps` and `/pricing`, all only when `dedicatedAccessFor(user).allowed`. Launch = Setting `dedicated_public_enabled=true`, no code change.
- **Logos:** `lib/dedicated/brand.ts` detects AMD / Intel / NVIDIA from CPU and GPU model strings; `components/dedicated/BrandLogo.tsx` renders `public/nxm/home/logos-{amd,intel,nvidia}.svg` (white lettering + brand accents), inverted with the hue turned back on the portal's light theme. Builds with a GPU show it (default GPU only; GPU options are not configurable yet).
- Same-metro locations now have distinct customer labels (France (North 1/2), France (Paris A/B/C)).

Tests: `test/dedicated-ops.test.ts` (every write path against the mock, guards, dry run, the real image list), `test/dedicated-gate.test.ts` (NXM page + nav gating), `test/dedicated-brand-voice.test.ts` (now also the NXM page and the control panel).

Tests: `test/preview-access.test.ts`, `test/dedicated-order.test.ts` (pure), `test/dedicated-gate.test.ts` (updated for the preview gate), and the opt-in DB test `test/dedicated-order-db.test.ts` (throwaway 127.0.0.1 `/dedprev` DB with a real read-only catalogue sync: gate + Settings overrides, displayed === charged, stock refusals, wallet placement once, card-leg fulfilment once with the stamped total, tampered stamps refused).

input.message:
URGENT: I stopped early to report a mistake on the shared Postgres cluster. It affects the prod `nxeon` database's owner. None of the bare-metal overhaul has been done yet. Please relay this to the owner now.

**What I did wrong**
- I made a throwaway DB for the work: new role `agt_baremetal`, then `createdb -O agt_baremetal -T nxeon_agt_dedicated nxeon_agt_baremetal`. That part was fine.
- I then ran `REASSIGN OWNED BY nxeon TO agt_baremetal` inside `nxeon_agt_baremetal`. I meant it to fix table ownership in my copy only.
- `REASSIGN OWNED` also moves cluster-wide shared objects, which includes database ownership. Every database the `nxeon` role owned is now owned by `agt_baremetal`:
  - `nxeon` (prod)
  - `nxeon_pb1007`
  - `nxeon_agt_modproviders`, `nxeon_agt_dedicated`, `nxeon_agt_ssl`, `nxeon_agt_cyrus`, `nxeon_agt_cyrustokens`, `nxeon_agt_adminshell`, `nxeon_agt_tours`, `nxeon_agt_nxlabs`, `nxeon_agt_adminmail`, `nxeon_agt_gamestate`
- No tables, rows or data in prod were touched. Only the database-level owner changed. Tables inside `nxeon` are still owned by `nxeon`.

**Why it matters**
- On PG15+ the `public` schema is owned by the database owner. So `nxeon` has probably lost CREATE on prod's `public` schema. A future `prisma db push` that adds tables (for example in `promote-production.sh`) may fail until this is fixed.
- `agt_baremetal` now owns prod. As schema owner it could drop objects there. The role is local, and its password is only in `/root/agent-notes/.baremetal-dburl` (root-only, mode 600). I have not used it against any DB except my throwaway.
- `https://nxeon.cloud/` and `/login` both return 200, so the live site looks up. I could not confirm DB connectivity, because the classifier also blocked my read-only check of `pg_database`.

**Fix (needs your approval to run; I tried and the auto-mode classifier blocked it)**
```
for d in nxeon nxeon_pb1007 nxeon_agt_modproviders nxeon_agt_dedicated nxeon_agt_ssl nxeon_agt_cyrus nxeon_agt_cyrustokens nxeon_agt_adminshell nxeon_agt_tours nxeon_agt_nxlabs nxeon_agt_adminmail nxeon_agt_gamestate; do su postgres -c "psql -Atc 'ALTER DATABASE \"$d\" OWNER TO nxeon'"; done
su postgres -c "psql -Atc \"select datname, pg_get_userbyid(datdba) from pg_database order by 1\""
```
After that, `agt_baremetal` should own only `nxeon_agt_baremetal`. Those 12 are exactly the databases that changed: the role had just been created, so anything it owns other than `nxeon_agt_baremetal` came from this command.

**State of the bare-metal task**
- Worktree `/tank/nxeon-wt-baremetal` exists on branch `feature/bare-metal-overhaul`, made from main at 7e4cda26e4. No code changes and no commits.
- `node_modules` there is a real directory of symlinks into `/tank/nxeon-wt-release2/node_modules`. It has its own copy of `@prisma/client` and its own generated `.prisma`. It is gitignored.
- Throwaway DB `nxeon_agt_baremetal` is a clone of `nxeon_agt_dedicated`: 240 catalogue items, 36,294 stock rows, users `admin@dev.local` / `customer@dev.local`.
- I've read the current code, and the plan is ready:
  - **Speed:** the catalogue and configure pages load every catalogue item, option and stock row on each request, and the owned-server page calls the supplier's live API while rendering. I'd cache the catalogue and load the live server status after the page appears.
  - **Card payment:** it already uses the same inline Stripe card form as VPS orders. I'd add the same Card / Wallet choice the VPS checkout shows.

URGENT: I stopped early to report a mistake on the shared Postgres cluster. It affects the prod `nxeon` database's owner. None of the bare-metal overhaul has been done yet. Please relay this to the owner now.

**What I did wrong**
- I made a throwaway DB for the work: new role `agt_baremetal`, then `createdb -O agt_baremetal -T nxeon_agt_dedicated nxeon_agt_baremetal`. That part was fine.
- I then ran `REASSIGN OWNED BY nxeon TO agt_baremetal` inside `nxeon_agt_baremetal`. I meant it to fix table ownership in my copy only.
- `REASSIGN OWNED` also moves cluster-wide shared objects, which includes database ownership. Every database the `nxeon` role owned is now owned by `agt_baremetal`:
  - `nxeon` (prod)
  - `nxeon_pb1007`
  - `nxeon_agt_modproviders`, `nxeon_agt_dedicated`, `nxeon_agt_ssl`, `nxeon_agt_cyrus`, `nxeon_agt_cyrustokens`, `nxeon_agt_adminshell`, `nxeon_agt_tours`, `nxeon_agt_nxlabs`, `nxeon_agt_adminmail`, `nxeon_agt_gamestate`
- No tables, rows or data in prod were touched. Only the database-level owner changed. Tables inside `nxeon` are still owned by `nxeon`.

**Why it matters**
- On PG15+ the `public` schema is owned by the database owner. So `nxeon` has probably lost CREATE on prod's `public` schema. A future `prisma db push` that adds tables (for example in `promote-production.sh`) may fail until this is fixed.
- `agt_baremetal` now owns prod. As schema owner it could drop objects there. The role is local, and its password is only in `/root/agent-notes/.baremetal-dburl` (root-only, mode 600). I have not used it against any DB except my throwaway.
- `https://nxeon.cloud/` and `/login` both return 200, so the live site looks up. I could not confirm DB connectivity, because the classifier also blocked my read-only check of `pg_database`.

**Fix (needs your approval to run; I tried and the auto-mode classifier blocked it)**
```
for d in nxeon nxeon_pb1007 nxeon_agt_modproviders nxeon_agt_dedicated nxeon_agt_ssl nxeon_agt_cyrus nxeon_agt_cyrustokens nxeon_agt_adminshell nxeon_agt_tours nxeon_agt_nxlabs nxeon_agt_adminmail nxeon_agt_gamestate; do su postgres -c "psql -Atc 'ALTER DATABASE \"$d\" OWNER TO nxeon'"; done
su postgres -c "psql -Atc \"select datname, pg_get_userbyid(datdba) from pg_database order by 1\""
```
After that, `agt_baremetal` should own only `nxeon_agt_baremetal`. Those 12 are exactly the databases that changed: the role had just been created, so anything it owns other than `nxeon_agt_baremetal` came from this command.

**State of the bare-metal task**
- Worktree `/tank/nxeon-wt-baremetal` exists on branch `feature/bare-metal-overhaul`, made from main at 7e4cda26e4. No code changes and no commits.
- `node_modules` there is a real directory of symlinks into `/tank/nxeon-wt-release2/node_modules`. It has its own copy of `@prisma/client` and its own generated `.prisma`. It is gitignored.
- Throwaway DB `nxeon_agt_baremetal` is a clone of `nxeon_agt_dedicated`: 240 catalogue items, 36,294 stock rows, users `admin@dev.local` / `customer@dev.local`.

20373:## Light theme rules — customer portal (2026-10-07 audit)
## Light theme rules — customer portal (2026-10-07 audit)

Audit of every `app/dashboard/**` page/tab/state in light mode (screens + findings: `/root/agent-notes/lightmode-audit/`). The portal was designed dark and light was added as a token swap, so what broke was whatever a token cannot reach. Rules so new pages do not regress:

**How the theme works.** `<html data-theme="light">` is set by `components/nx/ThemeToggle.tsx` (localStorage `nx-theme`, pre-applied by the inline script in `app/layout.tsx`, dashboard routes only). Tokens are re-declared in `:root.nx-portal[data-theme="light"]` (app/globals.css): the slate ramp and `navy-*` ramp are INVERTED (50 = ink, 950 = paper) and `--color-white` is ink. Dark chrome that must stay dark in both themes (rail, top bar, heroes, consoles, dark modals) carries `.nx-dark-island`, which re-declares the dark tokens for its subtree.

**Do**
- Use tokens: `text-tx`, `text-tx-dim`, `text-tx-faint`, `bg-surface`, `bg-well`, `border-rim-hi`, `text-mint|amber|cyan|rose|violet`. They are measured for AA on white / `--color-well` / `--color-bg` in light.
- A surface that is dark in both themes (terminal, hero over a photo, dark modal): put `nx-dark-island` on it. Do not rely on `bg-[rgba(3,9,24,…)]` staying dark — light mode turns those into wells.
- A label on a SOLID brand fill: write `text-[#fff]` (literal white). Plain `text-white` follows `--color-white`, which is ink in light. (`text-white` on `bg-brand-500` / `bg-[linear-gradient(…#hex…)]` is auto-corrected, but do not depend on it.)
- Switch thumbs: `bg-white rounded-full transition-*` is auto-kept white.
- Native controls (`select`, date inputs): never write `[color-scheme:dark]`; `color-scheme` follows the theme.

**Do not** hard-code a pastel (`text-[#a892ff]`, `text-red-300`, `text-emerald-400`) expecting it to read on white — see "generated" below — and never add a blanket `[class*="bg-white/"]` selector: it also matches `hover:`/`sm:` variants and paints them permanently.

**Generated light counterparts — `scripts/gen-light-literals.mjs` → `app/light-literals.generated.css`** (imported at the top of globals.css; do not hand-edit):
1. every `text-[#hex]` (pastel/mid range), dark `bg-[#hex]`, dark `border-[#hex]` literal found in `app/` + `components/` gets a light value (same hue, lightness lowered to ≥ 4.5:1 on white);
2. every exact `bg-white/N`, `border-white/N`, `text-white/N` token, including `hover:`/`focus:`/`group-hover:`/`sm:` forms, gets a wash of ink at an alpha mapped from N (so a 2% stripe and a 20% highlight stay different);
3. Tailwind palette shades 100–400 (`text-red-300`, `text-emerald-400`, …) are re-declared darker in the light scope and restored to stock inside `.nx-dark-island`.
Run `node scripts/gen-light-literals.mjs` after adding a new literal; `node scripts/check-light-theme.mjs` (also `npm test` → `test/light-theme.test.ts`) fails when the generated file is stale or when a new near-black `bg-[rgba(r,g,b,…)]`, inline dark `background`, or bare `bg-black` appears in the portal with no override / `nx-dark-island`. Hand-written pattern overrides (selected tab pills, danger chips, wells…) live in the "LIGHT THEME — PASS 2" block at the end of globals.css.

**Verify** in a browser, both themes, 1440 and 390: `localStorage.setItem("nx-theme","light")` then reload. Check selected/active states, disabled states, hover rows, empty and error states, modals, and third-party embeds (Stripe Elements follow `currentStripeAppearance()`; the VNC/xterm consoles are intentionally dark).

## Dedicated servers: catalogue, pricing, managed machines, previews (2026-10-06, branch `feature/dedicated-servers`)

Resold bare-metal, built so the owner can review everything before customers see any of it. **Unreleased by default**: Setting `dedicated_public_enabled` is `false`, so `/dedicated-servers` and `/dashboard/dedicated/**` 404 for everyone except **private-preview accounts** (see "Private preview + online checkout" below; fail closed if settings cannot be read) and the sitemap does not list them. Admins review both at `/admin/preview/dedicated` and `/admin/preview/dedicated/dashboard`. The portal rail shows a "Dedicated" entry only to viewers who pass the gate.

**Brand voice.** Customers never see the supplier's name, ranges, plan codes, service names, datacenter codes or URLs. Upstream identity lives only in admin pages and in `lib/dedicated/ovh-catalog.ts` / `sync.ts` / `catalog-view.ts`. Customer components (`components/dedicated/**`, the two customer route trees) only read `lib/dedicated/customer-view.ts` projections. Those projections copy a field whitelist, pass free text through `brandSafe()`, and hide the supplier's default `nsNNN.ip-a-b-c.tld` hostname. `test/dedicated-brand-voice.test.ts` checks the source files and the real output built from recorded catalogue fixtures.

**Catalogue sync** (`lib/dedicated/sync.ts`; worker sweep `dedicated-catalog`, 1-minute wake, self-throttled; admin "Sync now"; `npx tsx scripts/dedicated-catalog-sync.ts [SUBSIDIARY]`):
- **Read-only.** Three anonymous GETs and no API keys: `/order/catalog/public/eco` and `/order/catalog/public/baremetalServers` (`?ovhSubsidiary=`), plus `/dedicated/server/datacenter/availabilities`. The host follows the subsidiary: WE/WS/ASIA/CA/... use `ca.api.ovh.com`, US uses `api.us.ovhcloud.com`, the EU subsidiaries use `eu.api.ovh.com`. `publicGet` refuses any other path. The default subsidiary is `WE` (our account's own, USD). Upstream prices are in units of 1e-8 of the currency, so cents = price / 1e6.
- **Data.**
  - `DedicatedCatalogItem` holds one row per upstream plan. Regional variants (`-sgp`, `-syd`, `-mum`) are separate plans with their own price.
  - `DedicatedCatalogOption` holds the memory, storage, system-storage, bandwidth, vrack and GPU choices, each with its extra monthly cost. Licences are skipped.
  - `DedicatedAvailability` is the stock snapshot per plan, memory and storage configuration and datacenter.
  - `DedicatedCatalogSync` records every attempt with its counts, warnings and errors.
- **Keep last good.**
  - Each catalogue is fetched, parsed and written independently. A parse that returns less than 30% of the plans we hold is treated as an upstream glitch, not as a mass removal. Plans that disappear get `removedAt` and are never deleted.
  - The stock snapshot is replaced in one transaction, and only when the new feed is plausible.
  - A plan can be listed in both catalogues (the Advance range is). The first catalogue in the run owns it.
- **Nxeon-owned columns** are never touched by a sync: `visible` (default false), `displayName`, markup overrides, `overrideMonthlyCents`, setup policy, `hiddenRegions` and `adminNote`.
- **First live run (2026-10-06, WE).** 240 unique plans (eco 99, baremetalServers 165, with overlap), 4,851 options and 36,294 stock rows. By range: Kimsufi 27, So you Start 13, Rise 35, Advance 42, Game 2, Scale 73, HGR 48. Datacenters: gra, fra, bhs, rbx, sbg, waw, lon, sgp, syd, ynm, eu-west-par-a/b/c and ca-east-tor-a, all mapped.

**Regions** (`lib/dedicated/regions.ts`) map upstream DC codes to Nxeon codes in the `lib/node-regions.ts` style: sgp→sgp1, bhs→bhs1, gra→gra1, rbx→rbx1, waw→waw1, fra→fra1, lon→lon1, sbg→sbg1, syd→syd1, ynm→bom1, vin→vin1, hil→hil1, ca-east-tor-a→tor1, eu-west-par-a/b/c→par1/2/3.
- Each region has an admin label and a customer label.
- `sold` means Nxeon already runs nodes in that metro (sgp1, bhs1).
- An unknown code maps to `unmapped:<code>`. It is flagged in the sync log and the admin catalogue, and nothing breaks.
- The regions where dedicated servers are offered come from Setting `dedicated_enabled_regions`. Default (owner decision 2026-10-06): **every mapped region**; only in-stock configurations are orderable. Untick regions on `/admin/dedicated/pricing`. (An existing Setting row from an earlier save keeps its old value.)

**Pricing** (`lib/dedicated/pricing.ts`, pure, `test/dedicated-pricing.test.ts`):
- The Nxeon price is `round(cost x (1 + markup%) + fixed)`. Every rounding mode rounds up: `ninety-nine` gives the next $X.99, and the other modes are `whole`, `five` and `none`.
- Item overrides win over the global rule. Options are marked up too, even on top of a hard override price.
- Setup-fee policy:
  - `pass` charges what the setup costs us now, including a live upstream promotion.
  - `waived` charges nothing.
  - `custom` charges a fixed fee.
- Settings: `dedicated_markup_percent` (25), `dedicated_markup_fixed_cents` (0), `dedicated_rounding` (ninety-nine), `dedicated_setup_policy` (pass), `dedicated_setup_custom_cents`. The defaults are placeholders pending the owner's decision.
- Cost, margin, first-year margin and setup payback are shown in admin only.

**Admin** (ADMIN role only; nav: Fleet → Dedicated servers):
- `/admin/dedicated` is the catalogue browser. It filters by text, range, region, minimum RAM, maximum price, in-stock, visible and removed, and shows the sync status and **Sync now**.
- `/admin/dedicated/catalog/[id]` is the item detail page:
  - the hardware, economics, upstream commitment terms and promotions;
  - each region's stock and offered/hidden flags;
  - the full stock matrix (memory x storage by datacenter) and every option with cost vs Nxeon price;
  - the Nxeon controls and "Create offer from this item".
- `/admin/dedicated/pricing` holds the rules, the offered regions (with "we have nodes" / "not sold yet"), the public-pages switch and a worked example table.
- `/admin/dedicated/servers` and `/admin/dedicated/servers/[id]` hold the managed machines (`DedicatedServer`):
  - Each record has the customer, frozen specs, Nxeon region, IPs, OS, renewal date/price/term, linked invoice ids, offer id, and **admin-only** fields (upstream service name, upstream DC, our cost, internal notes).
  - The manual lifecycle is PENDING → PROVISIONING → ACTIVE ⇄ SUSPENDED → CANCELLED. It **records state only**; staff do the real work by hand.
  - Credential delivery is encrypted with `lib/crypto-box`, and the customer reveals the credentials themselves.

content.thinking:
I'm figuring out how to classify machines into product families based on total CPU cores (cores times count) and GPU presence—mapping high core/socket counts to "NX-Titan", GPUs to "NX-GPU", and high-clock consumer desktop chips like Ryzen or Core i7 to "NX-Pulse".

I'm also drawing a legacy line for older CPUs (pre-2020-ish Ryzen/Intel generations, older Xeon E3/E5/D series) which should map to the "Core" tier instead of newer families, while modern server chips like EPYC 4004/4005 and newer Xeon-E land in "NX-Forge". I'm sketching a naming convention combining family, core count, and RAM, like "NX-Forge 8-64", though I'm unsure about the exact suffix format.

For collisions where two different hardware builds produce the same name, I'll append a vendor letter (A/I for AMD/Intel), then a storage medium letter, then a sequence number, computed across the whole catalogue so disambiguation stays consistent and cacheable, storing results in a map keyed by hardware signature.

But a purely local naming scheme can still collide—two different same-spec CPU variants would both land on identical names—so I need a global disambiguation pass, probably ordered by price. The problem is this introduces order-dependence: if stock changes and a build drops out of the catalogue, the remaining names could shift, which is bad for stability.

Appending the raw CPU model string isn't ideal since the owner wants proprietary naming, not CPU names. I'll disambiguate collisions by computing stable suffixes over the full live catalogue (regardless of stock, since the snapshot only excludes items with zero offered regions), assigning letter-based suffixes in a deterministic sort order rather than exposing CPU codes directly.

Now I'm defining the pure tagging logic: marking cards as "New" based on firstSeenAt thresholds, computing "Best value" via a cost-per-unit score favoring cores and RAM among in-stock non-GPU cards, and flagging "High performance" using a threads-times-clock-speed metric for the top decile.

For "Most popular," I'm prioritizing pinned items, falling back to builds with at least 3 paid orders in the last 180 days, and defaulting to none if neither condition is met.

For pricing, I need an uplift percentage setting with a default of 10%, applied to the raw sell price calculation that factors in base cost, options, fixed costs, and markup percentage, with options rounded up when overridden.

Extra IPs priced separately from dedicated_ip_price_cents aren't affected by this. content.thinking:
I'm noticing too many letter suffixes piling up in names like "NX-Core 4-32i" since disambiguation is happening across all items regardless of storage class. I should fold storage class into the model code itself so collisions are reduced, reserving letters as a last-resort tiebreaker.

Thinking through alternatives: maybe append a storage descriptor like "/4T" or a readable tag such as "· 2×2TB" instead of raw letters, or decide the base name can repeat since the subtitle already shows CPU and storage details. But duplicate proprietary names would confuse invoices and reviews, so I'm settling on: base name as family plus cores-ram, and only when there's a true collision, append a storage-based suffix like "NV" for NVMe or "SSD" rather than an arbitrary letter.

Given the time constraints, I'll stick with the deterministic letter-suffix scheme for collisions rather than overcomplicating it with medium codes or numeric generations—it's simple and documented, even if some resulting names like "NX-Forge 16-128b" look a bit odd.

I'm also checking older EPYC chips: 7351p, 7371, 7451 (Zen 1 Naples) and 7313, 7402, 7413 (Zen 2/3) all classify as Forge, which seems acceptable. I'll flag Naples (7xx1) as legacy, but since the rule still routes legacy chips with enough cores and server-class status into Forge, the classification stays consistent.

The best-value tagging for Core builds and high-performance tagging for Titans both look correct since they track top CPU class appropriately. Caching performance checks out too — 0ms cached, 1.7s first build.

Now I'm moving to tiers.ts, which feeds into customer-view's toPublicCatalogEntry function. I need to update that function to use the new nxFamily and name fields, and set a default server label.

/**
 * CUSTOMER-FACING: the bare-metal hero illustration. Original vector art in the
 * Nxeon palette (navy, violet #7b3fef -> blue #3b6be8, cyan accents): a
 * single-tenant rack with live status LEDs, a CPU die lifted out of it, and
 * traffic flowing between them. No stock imagery, no supplier marks.
 *
 * Motion is CSS only (components/dedicated/bm.css: .bm-art .led / .pkt /
 * .float / .scan / .glow) and switches off under prefers-reduced-motion.
 * Server component: no client JS.
 */
export function BareMetalHeroArt({ className = "" }: { className?: string }) {
  const units = Array.from({ length: 7 }, (_, i) => i);
  return (
    <svg viewBox="0 0 560 340" className={"bm-art " + className} role="img" aria-label="Illustration: a bare metal server rack with a processor and network traffic">
      <defs>
        <linearGradient id="bmA" x1="0" y1="0" x2="1" y2="1">
          <stop offset="0" stopColor="#8b6cff" />
          <stop offset="1" stopColor="#3b6be8" />
        </linearGradient>
        <linearGradient id="bmRack" x1="0" y1="0" x2="0" y2="1">
          <stop offset="0" stopColor="#1a2336" />
          <stop offset="1" stopColor="#0c1220" />
        </linearGradient>
        <linearGradient id="bmSide" x1="0" y1="0" x2="1" y2="0">
          <stop offset="0" stopColor="#0b1120" />
          <stop offset="1" stopColor="#141c2e" />
        </linearGradient>
        <linearGradient id="bmUnit" x1="0" y1="0" x2="1" y2="0">
          <stop offset="0" stopColor="#222c42" />
          <stop offset="1" stopColor="#182033" />
        </linearGradient>
        <radialGradient id="bmHalo" cx="0.5" cy="0.5" r="0.5">
          <stop offset="0" stopColor="#8b6cff" stopOpacity="0.55" />
          <stop offset="1" stopColor="#8b6cff" stopOpacity="0" />
        </radialGradient>
        <linearGradient id="bmScan" x1="0" y1="0" x2="0" y2="1">
          <stop offset="0" stopColor="#5ad7ff" stopOpacity="0" />
          <stop offset="0.5" stopColor="#5ad7ff" stopOpacity="0.55" />
          <stop offset="1" stopColor="#5ad7ff" stopOpacity="0" />
        </linearGradient>
        <clipPath id="bmFace"><rect x="150" y="40" width="170" height="262" rx="10" /></clipPath>
      </defs>

      {/* floor glow */}
      <ellipse cx="270" cy="312" rx="230" ry="20" fill="#3b6be8" opacity="0.16" />
      <ellipse cx="240" cy="310" rx="120" ry="9" fill="#000" opacity="0.45" />

      {/* traffic lines (behind) */}
      <g fill="none" strokeLinecap="round">
        <path d="M320 112 C 380 112, 380 92, 430 92" stroke="#2c3a5c" strokeWidth="2" />
        <path d="M320 178 C 395 178, 400 200, 470 210" stroke="#2c3a5c" strokeWidth="2" />
        <path d="M150 140 C 90 140, 80 170, 36 176" stroke="#2c3a5c" strokeWidth="2" />
        <path className="pkt" d="M320 112 C 380 112, 380 92, 430 92" stroke="#5ad7ff" strokeWidth="2.4" strokeDasharray="14 106" />
        <path className="pkt p2" d="M320 178 C 395 178, 400 200, 470 210" stroke="#8b6cff" strokeWidth="2.4" strokeDasharray="14 106" />
        <path className="pkt p3" d="M150 140 C 90 140, 80 170, 36 176" stroke="#5ad7ff" strokeWidth="2.4" strokeDasharray="14 106" />
      </g>

      {/* rack: side panel + face */}
      <path d="M320 40 L350 26 L350 288 L320 302 Z" fill="url(#bmSide)" />
      <path d="M150 40 L180 26 L350 26 L320 40 Z" fill="#202a40" />
      <rect x="150" y="40" width="170" height="262" rx="10" fill="url(#bmRack)" stroke="#2a3550" />
      <g clipPath="url(#bmFace)">
        {units.map((i) => {
          const y = 54 + i * 34;
          const led = ["l1", "l2", "l3", "l4"][i % 4];
          return (
            <g key={i}>
              <rect x="162" y={y} width="146" height="26" rx="5" fill="url(#bmUnit)" stroke="#2c3854" />
              {Array.from({ length: 9 }, (_, k) => (
                <rect key={k} x={212 + k * 9} y={y + 8} width="4" height="10" rx="1.5" fill="#0d1322" />
              ))}
              <circle className={`led ${led}`} cx="174" cy={y + 13} r="3" fill={i === 2 ? "#8b6cff" : "#2fd39a"} />
              <circle className={`led ${["l3", "l4", "l1", "l2"][i % 4]}`} cx="186" cy={y + 13} r="2.2" fill="#5ad7ff" opacity="0.9" />
              <rect x="294" y={y + 9} width="7" height="8" rx="1.5" fill="#2a3550" />
            </g>
          );
        })}
        <rect className="scan" x="150" y="40" width="170" height="40" fill="url(#bmScan)" />
      </g>
      <rect x="150" y="40" width="170" height="262" rx="10" fill="none" stroke="url(#bmA)" strokeOpacity="0.35" />

      {/* CPU die, lifted out of the rack */}
      <g className="float">
        <circle className="glow" cx="455" cy="96" r="70" fill="url(#bmHalo)" />
        <g transform="translate(455 96) rotate(-8)">
          {[-26, -13, 0, 13, 26].map((o) => (
            <g key={o} stroke="#6e7fa8" strokeWidth="2.4" strokeLinecap="round">
              <path d={`M${o} -44 V -36`} /><path d={`M${o} 36 V 44`} />
              <path d={`M-44 ${o} H -36`} /><path d={`M36 ${o} H 44`} />
            </g>
          ))}
          <rect x="-36" y="-36" width="72" height="72" rx="10" fill="#141c2e" stroke="url(#bmA)" strokeWidth="2" />
          <rect x="-22" y="-22" width="44" height="44" rx="6" fill="url(#bmA)" opacity="0.92" />
          <path d="M-10 -6 h20 M-10 0 h14 M-10 6 h20" stroke="#fff" strokeOpacity="0.85" strokeWidth="2.2" strokeLinecap="round" />
        </g>
      </g>

      {/* memory stick */}
      <g className="float f2">
        <g transform="translate(492 214) rotate(10)">
          <rect x="-42" y="-11" width="84" height="22" rx="3" fill="#16203a" stroke="#3b6be8" strokeOpacity="0.7" />
          {[-30, -16, -2, 12, 26].map((x) => <rect key={x} x={x} y="-6" width="10" height="12" rx="1.5" fill="#24314f" />)}
          <path d="M-36 11 v4 M-26 11 v4 M-16 11 v4 M-6 11 v4 M4 11 v4 M14 11 v4 M24 11 v4 M34 11 v4" stroke="#c9a54a" strokeWidth="1.6" />
        </g>
      </g>

      {/* network endpoint */}
      <g>
        <circle cx="30" cy="177" r="15" fill="#0f1729" stroke="#2c3a5c" strokeWidth="2" />
        <circle cx="30" cy="177" r="6" fill="#5ad7ff" className="glow" />
      </g>
    </svg>
  );
}

I should verify the "star" icon exists in NX_ICONS. Now I'm designing the catalogue component's props and layout, keeping filter state local since the component stays mounted while configuring, and sketching the hero section with an eyebrow label and heading.

Below that I'm planning the stats row with real numbers like stock count, locations, starting price, and delivery time, plus brand logos and a hero art element. Then the filter card follows with search, brand/family toggles, region chips with flags, range sliders for price/cores/memory/storage, a live result counter with reset, a toolbar for sort and view mode, and finally the card design itself showing family tags, server name, and CPU details with brand logo.

Now I'm fleshing out card footer and list view layouts, plus defining stepped slider scales for price, cores, RAM, and storage so each range uses sensible discrete increments rather than continuous values, with the top slot representing "no upper limit."

For filtering logic, I'm checking whether a card's range intersects the selected slider bounds, and considering using maxRamGb so upgradable RAM configurations count toward matches. I'm also planning sort options (price, cores, memory, storage, best value), pagination with a "Show more" button showing 24 at a time, and wiring up the Configure button to trigger a callback.

Now I'm thinking through the payment step of the configurator — two method tiles, Card and Wallet, where Wallet is disabled or partial when the balance doesn't cover the full total, and I need to simplify how partial wallet coverage plus card payment for the remainder gets presented.

Selecting a card option triggers a request to create the checkout session, mounting the Stripe fields; switching tiles needs to invalidate the old session so I don't end up recreating it repeatedly, so I'll key session creation off the selected useWallet value and only create it while on the pay step. I'm also deciding whether to merge the review and pay steps or keep the stepper as Choose → Configure → Review → Pay.

On the pay step, changing the method should re-fetch the quote with the updated useWallet flag so the split updates, while I compute the walletApplied amount client-side (min(balance, total) if wallet is used) purely for display — the server handles the actual split logic. I should check the wallet-split library in case there's a minimum card charge rule to account for.

I'm planning the marketing page overhaul, starting with the hero section: an eyebrow pill, a bold H1 about bare metal servers being "yours alone," a supporting lede, dual CTAs linking to the catalogue and VPS comparison, and a "Powered by" logo strip.

For the hero art, I want a single source of truth—generating the SVG as a string in a shared lib function so both the React component and the NXM loader can render identical markup, reusing the same animation keyframes in both CSS files. I also want to check whether NXM marketing has a light theme, since the white logo lettering only works cleanly on dark backgrounds.

Now I'm planning the rest of the page structure: upgrading the catalogue filters with flag chips, brand toggles, and range sliders; adding a family explainer section with real pricing; a how-it-works section; a VPS comparison table; a locations section linking to SEO region pages; an FAQ with schema markup; and replacing the redundant pre-footer section with something that reuses the homepage's background treatment instead of duplicating the catalogue/pricing content.

For that final section, I'm thinking "One account for everything" as the eyebrow, with a headline about running bare metal alongside VPS, game servers, and domains under the same dashboard and billing — framing bare metal as an upgrade path from VPS rather than a custom build offer. CTAs would point to account creation and the VPS page, with a supporting line about full root access, DDoS protection, and 24-hour provisioning, and I'm starting to sketch the meta title for SEO.

For the description and OG tags, I want real pricing and location counts, but I need to be careful since generateMetadata runs before the catalogue is gated — if the page isn't public and triggers a 404, leaking pricing data through metadata could be risky, so I should keep the static text number-free unless the feature is confirmed public, and check how the existing SEO helpers handle Open Graph.

Now I'm thinking through the structured data needs: beyond the existing Product/AggregateOffer, I should add FAQPage, BreadcrumbList, and an ItemList of top offers each with real Product/Offer pricing. # Part VII — Change history

Everything below this line is **history**, not reference. It is kept because the *reasons* recorded in
these entries are often the only surviving explanation for why a piece of code looks the way it does.
Where an entry contradicts Parts I–VI, **Parts I–VI win** — they were verified against the tree; these
were written at the time.

## How to read the change history

```
 Part VII is ordered oldest → newest in three layers:
   1. "Change history — the first 28 commits"   the compressed early record
   2. dated / titled entries                    one H2 per shipped change
   3. "Session log — 2026-07-26/27"             the most recent waves
 Authoritative alternatives when an entry looks stale:
   git log --date=short --pretty='%h|%ad|%s'
   git blame <file> -L <start>,<end>
```

## Bare Metal overhaul (2026-10-07, branch `feature/bare-metal-overhaul`)

Owner requests 2026-10-07, built on top of the dedicated-servers preview above. **Still a private preview**: every surface below keeps the `lib/dedicated/gate.ts` gate (public flag `dedicated_public_enabled` OR the preview allowlist), fails closed, and is noindex / out of the sitemap until launch.

**Naming.** Customer-facing copy says **Bare Metal Dedicated Servers** (nav "Bare Metal", page titles, invoices `Bare Metal Dedicated Server — <label>`, notifications, the `dedicated_server_ready` email in `prisma/seed-email-templates.ts` + `lib/email-render.ts` fallback). Marketing keeps both "bare metal" and "dedicated servers" wording for SEO. Admin pages keep "Dedicated".

**IA.**
- `/dashboard/dedicated` IS the order flow (`components/dedicated/flow/BareMetalFlow.tsx`): catalogue → configure → review → pay. There is no "you have no servers" page any more.
- `/dashboard/dedicated/order` and `/dashboard/dedicated/order/<id>` are gated redirects to `/dashboard/dedicated` and `/dashboard/dedicated?build=<id>[&region=]` (old links and the NXM "Configure" links keep working).
- A customer's machines live under **My Services** (`lib/nx/services.ts` kind `"dedicated"`, tab "Bare Metal" shown only when the account has one) and in the dashboard home **Services** card (`app/dashboard/page.tsx`, filter pill "Bare Metal"). Both read `lib/dedicated/services-rows.ts` `bareMetalRows(user)`, which returns `[]` unless the gate passes, and keeps the route strings inside the feature (the gate test's "nothing outside links to it" rule).
- The rail entry (`lib/dedicated/nav.ts`) is "Bare Metal" with the new `bmrack` icon; `NavItem.subActive` (generic, `lib/nx/nav.ts` + `components/nx/Shell.tsx`) lights **My Services** on an owned server page (`/dashboard/dedicated/<id>`).

**Performance** (the "configure → back to catalogue is slow" report).
- Cause: every catalogue/configure request read all live items, ~5k options and ~36k stock rows and rebuilt the merged cards (`loadOrderCatalog` ≈ 0.6-1.0 s per request on the shared box, 2.5 s worst), and "back" was a full server navigation that paid it again. The owned-server page also awaited live upstream status reads in its render path.
- `lib/dedicated/catalog-snapshot.ts`: an in-process snapshot of the catalogue reused while it is < 60 s old AND a cheap stamp (newest sync row, newest item edit, pricing settings, visible count) is unchanged (re-checked at most every 5 s). Derived cards/builds/names are memoised per snapshot. Warm `loadOrderCatalog` = 0 ms, `loadOrderBuild` = 0 ms. **The charge path never reads it**: `quoteDedicatedOrder` re-prices from the DB at Review and at Pay, so displayed-on-Review === charged.
- The flow is one client component: the catalogue stays mounted (hidden) while a build is configured, so filters/layout/scroll come back instantly; `?build=` is pushed onto history so Back/refresh/links work; builds come from the gated `loadDedicatedBuildAction` (prefetched on card hover/focus, cached per visit).
- The server page renders from our own row; `useDedicatedControls` loads the live panel after paint with skeletons. `loading.tsx` skeletons for the flow and the server page.

**Pay with Stripe.** The Pay step offers **Card** (the full amount through the same Stripe Custom Checkout session + inline `NxCardFields` form the VPS/game deploy wizard uses), **Wallet balance** (when it covers the total) and **Balance + card** (when it partly does). Server split via `walletSplit`, fulfilment unchanged (`lib/fulfil-checkout.ts` `dedicatedOrder`). Verified in Stripe TEST mode only (staging test keys, card 4242).

**Customer server dashboard** (`components/dedicated/DedicatedServerDashboard.tsx`, VpsPanelShell-shaped: pinned dark identity hero + `?tab=` rail): Overview (status timeline while building, live status, hardware tiles, IPs, login, plan, recent actions), Power & rescue, Reinstall, Network & IPs (addresses, rDNS + firewall, **buy extra IPv4** with card or wallet), Plan & billing (build, term, renewal date, renewal price as charged, extra IPs, setup fee, invoices, **Request cancellation** → `DedicatedServerRequest` kind `CANCEL` + support ticket; staff confirm the end date — no automatic cancellation/refund), Support. Controls are `components/dedicated/DedicatedControlPanel.tsx` sections sharing one `useDedicatedControls` state; they still only enqueue `DedicatedJob`s (dry run by default, mock in dev).

**Pricing.** See "Pricing" above: `dedicated_price_uplift_percent` (default 10) multiplies the marked-up price. Worked examples (cost → old → new): $107.00 → $133.99 → $147.99; $331.00 → $413.99 → $455.99. Editable on `/admin/dedicated/pricing` ("Price uplift % on top of markup").

**NX names** (`lib/dedicated/nx-names.ts`, pure, `test/dedicated-nx-names.test.ts`). Family by the first matching rule: NX-GPU (GPU fitted) → NX-Titan (32+ total cores or dual socket) → NX-Pulse (current high-clock desktop CPU: Ryzen 5000+, X3D, Core 10th gen+) → NX-Forge (current server CPU: EPYC, Xeon Gold/Silver/6, Xeon-E 23xx+, or 12+ cores) → NX-Core (earlier-generation/entry). Model code `<total cores>-<default RAM GB>` (e.g. `NX-Forge 8-64`). Builds that would share a name get a/b/c… ordered by CPU model then storage, computed over every live item (not just in-stock), so names do not move with stock. An admin `displayName` still wins. The real CPU and specs are always shown.

**Tags** (`lib/dedicated/tags.ts`, pure, `test/dedicated-tags.test.ts`), computed once over the in-stock catalogue: **Most popular** = admin pin (`DedicatedCatalogItem.popularPinned`, checkbox on the catalogue item page) else the build with the most paid orders in 180 days if ≥ 3; **Recommended** (only when neither exists, never labelled "popular") = cheapest in-stock NX-Forge with ≥ 64 GB; **Best value** = lowest 10% price per (cores + RAM GB/8); **High performance** = top 10% by threads × boost clock; **GPU**; **New** = first seen in the last 30 days and ≥ 7 days after the first sync. Max two per card.

**Design.** `components/dedicated/bm.css`, scoped under `.bm`: neutral graphite (dark) / white (light, `:root[data-theme="light"] .bm`) surfaces, a clear ink ramp, violet→blue accent only for selection, primary action and price; always-dark `bm-hero bm-island` regions; keyframes at top level; `prefers-reduced-motion` stops all motion. Hero art: original SVG (`lib/dedicated/hero-art.ts`, shared with NXM). Filter card: location chips with **bundled SVG flags** (`lib/dedicated/flags.ts`, hand-drawn, no CDN), AMD/Intel/NVIDIA logo toggles, NX class chips, dual-thumb range sliders (price, cores, memory, storage), search, live count, reset; card and list views (remembered per browser).

**Icons.** `bmrack`, `bmblade`, `bmchip`, `bmgpu`, `bmstack` in `lib/nx/icon-paths.ts` (violet tone, so bare metal never reads as a blue VPS mark); service mark `public/nx/svc/baremetal.svg` and card plate `public/nx/preview/baremetal.svg` (`SvcIcon name="baremetal"`).

**No custom builds.** Every "Ask for a custom build" / "Request this build" / "source a specific machine" CTA was removed (portal, legacy marketing page, NXM page, FAQ now says unlisted hardware can't be ordered).

**Marketing (NXM) `/dedicated-servers`** (`tools/nxm/native/dedicated-servers/*` → `python3 tools/nxm/port_pages.py dedicated-servers`; loader `app/nxm/_data/dedicated-servers.ts`): hero with the shared art and large AMD (Ryzen · EPYC) / Intel (Xeon) / NVIDIA logo tiles, the same filter card, card/list view, an "NX classes" section with real counts and from-prices, what you get, how it works, bare metal vs VPS, locations with flags (linking to country pages), FAQ (FAQPage JSON-LD from the markup), and a closing section on the **homepage's own bottom background** (`/nxm/home/cloud.webp` + the `.final` overlays, mirrored as `.dd-final`) replacing the old "Choose a build / See all pricing" block.
- **Country pages** `/dedicated-servers/<country>` (`app/nxm/dedicated-servers/[country]/page.tsx`, hand-written; list in `lib/dedicated/regions.ts` `DEDICATED_COUNTRY_PAGES`): "Bare Metal Dedicated Servers in Singapore" etc., same body with the country's own title/meta/H1/catalogue (pre-filtered), breadcrumb trail, and a 404 when the country has nothing offered. In `live-routes.json`; excluded from the NXM sitemap list (`DEDICATED_MARKETING_PATHS`) and added by `dedicatedSitemapPaths()` only when public.
- Structured data: Product + AggregateOffer (real low/high) and an ItemList of up to 12 in-stock builds, each a Product with a real monthly Offer.
- Internal links (all gated by `dedicatedAccessFor`, `app/nxm/_components/dedicated-nav.ts`): nav tab "Bare Metal", Products-menu "Bare Metal Dedicated Servers", mobile sheet, the "Need more power?" strip on /vps, /pricing and now /game-servers, and a homepage strip before its final section (`withDedicatedHome`).

**Site title (separate commit, gated).** `lib/dedicated/site-title.ts`; `app/layout.tsx`, `app/nxm/page.tsx` and `app/page.tsx` switch only when `dedicated_public_enabled` is on. Before launch the strings are byte-identical to before (`test/dedicated-site-title.test.ts`).

**Schema (additive):** `DedicatedCatalogItem.popularPinned Boolean @default(false)`. **Settings:** `dedicated_price_uplift_percent` (default `"10"`).

**Verification.** Throwaway DB `nxeon_agt_baremetal` (clone of the dedicated preview DB) + a scratch Postgres on 127.0.0.1:55447 for `test/dedicated-order-db.test.ts` (8/8: displayed === charged, wallet once, card leg once, tampered stamps refused, worker tick). Upstream in mock mode, dry run on. Stripe test mode only. Screens: `/root/agent-notes/bare-metal/`.
EOF

entries.name: Monitor
entries.description:
Start a background monitor that streams events from a long-running script. Each stdout line is an event — you keep working and notifications arrive in the chat. Events arrive on their own schedule and are not replies from the user, even if one lands while you're waiting for the user to answer a question.

Pick by how many notifications you need:
- **One** ("tell me when the server is ready / the build finishes") → use **Bash with `run_in_background`** and a command that exits when the condition is true, e.g. `until grep -q "Ready in" dev.log; do sleep 0.5; done`. You get a single completion notification when it exits.
- **One per occurrence, until the monitor expires (re-arm to continue)** ("tell me every time an ERROR line appears") → Monitor with an unbounded command (`tail -f`, `inotifywait -m`, `while true`).
- **One per occurrence, until a known end** ("emit each CI step result, stop when the run completes") → Monitor with a command that emits lines and then exits.

Your script's stdout is the event stream. Each line becomes a notification. Exit ends the watch.

  # Each matching log line is an event
  tail -f /var/log/app.log | grep --line-buffered "ERROR"

  # Each file change is an event
  inotifywait -m --format '%e %f' /watched/dir

  # Poll GitHub for new PR comments and emit one line per new comment
  last=$(date -u +%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%SZ)
  while true; do
    now=$(date -u +%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%SZ)
    gh api "repos/owner/repo/issues/123/comments?since=$last" --jq '.[] | "\(.user.login): \(.body)"'
    last=$now; sleep 30
  done

  # Node script that emits events as they arrive (e.g. WebSocket listener)
  node watch-for-events.js

  # Per-occurrence with a natural end: emit each CI check as it lands, exit when the run completes
  prev=""
  while true; do
    s=$(gh pr checks 123 --json name,bucket)
    cur=$(jq -r '.[] | select(.bucket!="pending") | "\(.name): \(.bucket)"' <<<"$s" | sort)
    comm -13 <(echo "$prev") <(echo "$cur")
    prev=$cur
    jq -e 'all(.bucket!="pending")' <<<"$s" >/dev/null && break
    sleep 30
  done

**Don't use an unbounded command for a single notification.** `tail -f`, `inotifywait -m`, and `while true` never exit on their own, so the monitor stays armed until timeout even after the event has fired. For "tell me when X is ready," use Bash `run_in_background` with an `until` loop instead (one notification, ends in seconds). Note that `tail -f log | grep -m 1 ...` does *not* fix this: if the log goes quiet after the match, `tail` never receives SIGPIPE and the pipeline hangs anyway.

**Script quality:**
- Every pipe stage must flush per line or matches sit in its buffer unseen: `grep` needs `--line-buffered`, `awk` needs `fflush()`. `head` cannot flush at all — `| head -N` delivers nothing until N matches accumulate, then ends the stream.
- In poll loops, handle transient failures (`curl ... || true`) — one failed request shouldn't kill the monitor.
- Poll intervals: 30s+ for remote APIs (rate limits), 0.5-1s for local checks.
- Write a specific `description` — it appears in every notification ("errors in deploy.log" not "watching logs").
- Only stdout is the event stream. Stderr goes to the output file (readable via Read) but does not trigger notifications — for a command you run directly (e.g. `python train.py 2>&1 | grep --line-buffered ...`), merge stderr with `2>&1` so its failures reach your filter. (No effect on `tail -f` of an existing log — that file only contains what its writer redirected.)

**Coverage — silence is not success.** When watching a job or process for an outcome, your filter must match every terminal state, not just the happy path. A monitor that greps only for the success marker stays silent through a crashloop, a hung process, or an unexpected exit — and silence looks identical to "still running." Before arming, ask: *if this process crashed right now, would my filter emit anything?* If not, widen it.

  # Wrong — silent on crash, hang, or any non-success exit
  tail -f run.log | grep --line-buffered "elapsed_steps="

  # Right — one alternation covering progress + the failure signatures you'd act on
  tail -f run.log | grep -E --line-buffered "elapsed_steps=|Traceback|Error|FAILED|assert|Killed|OOM"

For poll loops checking job state, emit on every terminal status (`succeeded|failed|cancelled|timeout`), not just success. If you cannot confidently enumerate the failure signatures, broaden the grep alternation rather than narrow it — some extra noise is better than missing a crashloop.

**Output volume**: Every stdout line is a conversation message, so the filter should be selective — but selective means "the lines you'd act on," not "only good news." Never pipe raw logs; filter to exactly the success and failure signals you care about. Monitors that produce too many events are automatically stopped; restart with a tighter filter if this happens.

Stdout lines within 200ms are batched into a single notification, so multiline output from a single event groups naturally.

The script runs in the same shell environment as Bash. Exit ends the watch (exit code is reported). Every monitor expires after `timeout_ms` (default 5 minutes, at most 30 minutes): it is killed and you get one notice with the event count. Re-arm it if you still need the watch; for a long watch (PR monitoring, log tails) set `timeout_ms` to the maximum and re-arm on each expiry, and widen the filter if an expiry with no events was unexpected. Use TaskStop to cancel early.
**ws source** — open a WebSocket and stream each incoming text frame as an event. No shell, no polling: the server pushes, you get notified.

  Monitor({
    ws: {url: 'wss://events.example.com/stream', protocols: ['v1']},
    description: 'deploy events',
  })

Each text frame becomes one notification (multiline frames stay as one event). Binary frames are reported as `[binary frame, N bytes]` rather than passed through. Socket close ends the watch with the close code surfaced; errors are surfaced before close. Same rate limiting as bash — a firehose will be suppressed and eventually stopped, so subscribe to a filtered feed where one exists.

Prefer this over `command: 'websocat wss://…'` — it avoids the extra process and line-buffering pitfalls. Use bash when you need to transform or filter frames with shell tools before they become events.

description.description: Short human-readable description of what you are monitoring (shown in notifications).

timeout_ms.description: Kill the monitor after this deadline. Default 300000ms. Deadlines above 1800000ms are capped to 1800000ms. You are notified at expiry and can re-arm.

command.description: Shell command or script. Each stdout line is an event; exit ends the watch.

ws.description: WebSocket to open. Each text frame is an event; binary frames are reported as a placeholder line. Socket close ends the watch. Cannot be combined with command.

The dev server seemed to crash at the homepage with a connection refused error, but then the Stripe test landed successfully afterward—so maybe the server restarted or the failure was just transient. I want to check the dev log to understand what actually happened.

The timings also look odd: catalogue→configure took 4364ms, and the back navigation took 2133ms instead of being instant. That delay makes me suspect Next.js is intercepting the popstate event from history.back() and triggering a real server-side RSC refetch rather than just a client-side state update, since Next 14+ syncs pushState with the router—meaning the back button could be causing an unnecessary server round-trip I need to find a way around.

Actually I bet the real culprit is loading.tsx — Next shows the Suspense fallback skeleton during the RSC navigation, replacing my catalogue entirely until the fetch resolves, which explains the 2-second delay. The fix is to stop letting Next's router intercept the pushState/popstate flow and handle the state restoration myself with plain window.history calls instead.

Actually, calling history.back() might not be ideal — I could instead set state directly and replaceState, though that loses the forward-entry semantics. I'm digging into Next's popstate handler and noticing it checks for a `__NA` flag on the state; if missing, it triggers a full page reload instead of a soft navigation, which could explain the slowness I'm seeing.

Next patches `pushState` to copy that `__NA` flag and the router tree into any state object, so my custom state should still carry it and avoid a reload — meaning the delay isn't coming from that reload path after all, so I need to look elsewhere for the 2-second lag.

Since I can't settle this through reasoning alone, I'll verify empirically: set a marker variable before navigating back and check whether it survives the back action, since a full reload would wipe it out.

I should run a targeted Playwright session — open the catalogue, click configure, set the mark, click back, then measure elapsed time and whether the mark persisted, plus capture whether a browser-level goBack triggers RSC requests. I also need to check the dev log since the server seems to have crashed at "/".

content.thinking:
The back navigation takes 357-403ms in-page, triggering a single RSC refetch since Next re-requests server data on search param changes. That delay likely comes from React re-rendering the large 24-card catalogue from hidden to visible, plus layout costs of un-hiding that content, rather than the state change itself being slow.

The real issue is that putting the build ID in search params causes Next to re-fetch the server render every time I open or close a configure panel — wasted work I could avoid by switching to hash-based state instead, since hash changes don't trigger Next's router fetch. The tradeoff is handling deep links and refreshes: with a hash, the server can't see it on initial load, so I'd need the client to read it on mount and fetch the build separately, while still supporting the existing `?build=` param for server-side deep links.

I'm trying to pin down exactly what's triggering that extra GET request, since it doesn't seem to come from Next's pushState patching itself — that path just restores the existing route tree without fetching. It's possible something else in my code, like a router.refresh() call or a component reading searchParams, is the real culprit.

Actually, I think I've found it: Next 15's page segment key encodes the search params directly, so when pushState changes the query string but the tree still has the old segment key, the router treats it as a missing segment and lazy-fetches it — that's the GET. The fix would be to move that client-side state into the URL hash instead of search params, since hash changes don't alter the segment key and won't trigger a refetch.

For deep links that arrive with `?build=` already set, the server renders the configurator directly, so going back to the catalogue means replacing the URL to drop that param — which does trigger one RSC fetch, but that's acceptable since it's rare and the state updates instantly anyway. I'm sketching the implementation: reading from the hash first (falling back to the initial search param), and having the configure action write `build` and `region` into the hash rather than the query string.

I also need popstate and hashchange listeners, and a back() handler that uses history.back() if there's bookmarked state, otherwise clears both hash and search manually.

On performance, dev mode render cost is around 350ms but production should be closer to 50ms, so I'll report both numbers honestly rather than just the dev figure.

For the mobile test failure — a locator.click timeout — I suspect something in the toolbar is covering the button, possibly a hidden "More filters" area; I want to check the dark mobile screenshot to see what's actually overlapping the AMD brand chip.
