All 10 requests and the 7 follow-up requests are built on branch `feature/bare-metal-overhaul` (worktree `/tank/nxeon-wt-baremetal`, 6 commits off main 7e4cda26e4). Everything is still behind the preview gate. Nothing is merged, deployed or pushed (the post-commit hook did not push the branch). tsc is clean and the dedicated tests pass.

**Earlier DB-ownership incident:** after your fix I only touched my own throwaway DBs. I used no cluster-wide role or ownership commands.

**What changed, per request**
1. **Rename:** customers now see "Bare Metal Dedicated Servers" everywhere: nav "Bare Metal", page titles, invoices (`Bare Metal Dedicated Server — <name>`), the Stripe line item, notifications and the server-ready email. Marketing keeps both "bare metal" and "dedicated servers" wording.
2. **Performance:**
   - The catalogue was loading every item, ~5k options and ~36k stock rows on every request. It is now cached in-process (`lib/dedicated/catalog-snapshot.ts`, 60 s, with a change check every 5 s). Payment always re-prices from the DB, so a stale display can never be charged.
   - Catalogue → configure → back now happens in the browser. The catalogue stays loaded, builds are prefetched on hover, and the URL uses `#build=`. With `?build=`, Next.js refetched the page on every open and Back; with the hash it makes no server request.
   - The owned-server page no longer waits for the live upstream reads; they load after the page appears. Loading skeletons added.
3. **Stripe:** the Pay step now offers Card, Wallet balance, or Balance + card, on the same Stripe checkout and inline card form as VPS/game orders. Verified end to end in TEST mode with card 4242:
   - Stripe session `livemode:false`, `paid`, $380.99.
   - Exactly one PENDING server and one PAID invoice were created.
   - The card amount was credited to the wallet and debited back once; the balance stayed at $50.00.
4. **IA:**
   - `/dashboard/dedicated` is now the catalogue → configure → review → pay flow. The old `/order` URLs redirect to it.
   - Owned servers appear in My Services (a "Bare Metal" tab, shown only when the account has one) and in the dashboard home Services card, whose Monthly Spend now includes them.
   - An owned server's page highlights My Services in the nav.
5. **Server dashboard:** tabbed like the VPS/game panels.
   - Overview: status, live status, hardware, IPs, login, plan.
   - Power & rescue and Reinstall: still dry-run only. The upstream is mocked in dev, so no real write was ever sent.
   - Network & IPs: rDNS, firewall and buying extra IPv4s by card or wallet.
   - Plan & billing: term, renewal date, renewal price as charged, setup fee, invoices, and a Request cancellation button that opens a ticket.
   - Support.
6. **Prices:** a new setting `dedicated_price_uplift_percent` (default 10, editable on `/admin/dedicated/pricing`) adds 10% on top of whatever markup is set.
7. **NX names:** deterministic, from the hardware only (`lib/dedicated/nx-names.ts`). The real CPU and specs are always shown. Nothing mentions the supplier.
8. **Tags:** Most popular, Recommended, Best value, High performance, GPU and New, with written rules in `lib/dedicated/tags.ts`. Most popular can be pinned by an admin on the catalogue item page (new additive column `popularPinned`).
9. **Design:** neutral graphite (dark) and white (light) surfaces, with the violet→blue accent only on selection, primary buttons and prices. Original animated SVG hero art that stops under reduced-motion. The filter card has hand-made SVG flags (no CDN), dual range sliders for price/cores/memory/storage, AMD/Intel/NVIDIA logo toggles, class chips, search, live count and reset. Card and list views.
10. **Icons:** a new set (`bmrack`, `bmblade`, `bmchip`, `bmgpu`, `bmstack`) plus a service mark and card image, used in the nav, My Services, the dashboard card and the catalogue.

**Follow-up requests**
- **Marketing page `/dedicated-servers`:** rebuilt in the same style:
  - Hero: large AMD (Ryzen · EPYC), Intel (Xeon) and NVIDIA logo tiles.
  - The same filter card, plus card and list views.
  - A section explaining the NX classes with real counts and prices.
- **Closing section:** the old "Choose a build / See all pricing" block is replaced by a section on the homepage's own bottom background (`cloud.webp` with its overlays).
- **Custom builds:** every "custom build" button and mention is gone. The FAQ now says unlisted hardware can't be ordered.
- **SEO:**
  - Country pages such as `/dedicated-servers/singapore` ("Bare Metal Dedicated Servers in Singapore"). Each 404s if the country has nothing on offer.
  - Product and per-build Offer structured data with real prices, plus the FAQ schema.
  - Internal links from the homepage, /vps, /pricing and /game-servers.
  - All gated: noindex and out of the sitemap until the launch flag is on.
- **Site title:** its own commit (da8d8be895). Nothing changes until `dedicated_public_enabled` is on:
  - Default title: "Nxeon — Cloud VPS Hosting, Game Servers & Domains" → "Nxeon — Cloud VPS Hosting, Game Servers, Dedicated Bare Metal Servers & Domains"
  - NXM homepage title: "Nxeon — Cloud VPS Hosting & Gaming Servers, live in 47 seconds." → "Nxeon — Cloud VPS, Gaming & Dedicated Bare Metal Servers"
  - Homepage description → "All-in-one cloud hosting: VPS live in 47 seconds, game servers, email and dedicated bare metal servers on enterprise hardware. Free migration, no lock-in."
  - Legacy homepage title: "Nxeon — Cloud VPS Hosting, live in 47 seconds." → "Nxeon — Cloud VPS, Game Servers & Dedicated Bare Metal Servers"
  - Site description: changed to a version naming dedicated bare metal servers; the exact before/after strings are in `lib/dedicated/site-title.ts`.

**Timings (before → after)**
| What | Before | After |
|---|---|---|
| Catalogue data load (same full catalogue, 104 builds) | 1,031 ms median (worst 2,562) | 0 ms warm, ~1.7 s on the first load after a change |
| Configure → back to catalogue | full server page load (~0.6 s server time in dev) | 200–330 ms, no server request, no reload |
| Browser Back from configure | full server page load | 270–430 ms |
| Reopening a build already viewed | full server page load | 240–360 ms |

These were measured on the dev server with the box at load ~15; I didn't run a production build because the shared lock was heavily contended. Full-page dev times aren't comparable between the two columns: the before page listed only 9 published items, the after page the full 104-build catalogue.

**Price examples (monthly, old → new)**
| Build | Old | New |
|---|---|---|
| EPYC 4244P, 32 GB | $133.99 | $147.99 |
| EPYC 4344P, 64 GB | $185.99 | $203.99 |
| EPYC 4584PX, 64 GB | $325.99 | $357.99 |
| Ryzen 7 9800X3D, 64 GB | $413.99 | $455.99 |
| Ryzen 7 5800X, 64 GB | $125.99 | $137.99 |
| Xeon-E3 1230v6, 16 GB | $23.99 | $25.99 |

A per-item hard price set by an admin is not uplifted, and existing machines keep their current renewal price.

**NX naming:** the name is the class plus `<total cores>-<RAM GB>`. When two different builds would share a name they get a/b/c, ordered by CPU model; this is worked out over the whole catalogue so names don't change with stock. Full list: `/root/agent-notes/bare-metal/nx-names.txt`.
| Class | Rule (first match wins) | Example |
|---|---|---|
| NX-GPU | a GPU is fitted | NX-GPU 16-192 (EPYC 9124 + 2× L4) |
| NX-Titan | 32+ total cores, or dual socket | NX-Titan 96-128b (EPYC Turin 9655) |
| NX-Pulse | current high-clock desktop CPU (Ryzen 5000+, X3D) | NX-Pulse 8-64c (Ryzen 7 9800X3D) |
| NX-Forge | current server CPU (EPYC, Xeon Gold/Silver/6, Xeon-E 23xx), or 12+ cores | NX-Forge 8-64a (EPYC 4344P) |
| NX-Core | older / entry hardware | NX-Core 4-16b (Xeon-E3 1230v6) |

**What's real vs test vs mocked**
- **Real:** the code paths, and the cached catalogue matching the charged price (the order DB test passed 8/8 in a scratch Postgres on :55447).
- **Test mode:** Stripe only.
- **Mocked:** the upstream supplier API (mock mode, dry run on).
- **Throwaway data:** DB `nxeon_agt_baremetal`. In it I un-published the 9 published items so the full catalogue shows, answered the "how did you hear about us" prompt for the test customer, and placed one test order.
- **Tests:** 88 pass across the dedicated tests, including new ones for names, tags, the uplift, the title gating and the gate. 22 failures in other test files are identical on a clean main checkout, so they were already failing.

**8 best screenshots** (all in `/root/agent-notes/bare-metal/`, 1440 + 390, dark + light):
- `01-catalogue-dark-desktop.png`
- `01-catalogue-light-desktop.png`
- `04-configure-dark-desktop.png`
- `07-pay-card-filled-test-mode-dark-desktop.png`
- `10-server-overview-light-desktop.png`
- `12-server-network-dark-mobile.png`
- `20-my-services-dark-desktop.png`
- `30-marketing-dark-desktop.png`

**Commits:** dc016e0957 (main work), da8d8be895 (gated title), 70ac6fdfb0, 97309c0430, 3770617965, 355fc71b7e. Docs (`docs/DOCUMENTATION.md`, section "Bare Metal overhaul (2026-10-07)" plus a change-history entry) and ROADMAP are updated.

**Decisions for the owner**
1. Is the 10% uplift right, and should a hard per-item price also get it?
2. Default "Most popular": with no pins and fewer than 3 orders in 180 days, the cheapest NX-Forge with 64 GB+ is labelled "Recommended", not "Most popular", to avoid claiming popularity without orders. Pin builds if you want "Most popular" shown.
3. Cancellation is a ticket; staff confirm the end date. Refund policy is still undefined.
4. Some NX names have letter suffixes (up to "i" on NX-Core 4-32). Keep them, or switch to a storage-based suffix?
5. Annual discount: none exists yet.
6. The existing public VPS page `/singapore-dedicated-server-hosting` overlaps the new bare-metal Singapore page in search. Point it at bare metal after launch?
7. Which builds to publish (mark visible) before launch.
8. Launch is still one switch: `dedicated_public_enabled`.
